Read a unified diff

Source: R/patch.R
patch_parse.Rd

Parses unified diff text, as diff_unified(), GNU diff -u and git diff write it, into one patch per file.

Usage

patch_parse(text)

Arguments

text

The unified diff, as one string.

Value

A list of file patches, each a list with old_name, new_name and hunks. Each hunk is a list with old_start, old_len, new_start and new_len, as in the @ header, and lines, a data frame with op ("equal", "delete" or "insert") and text, the line with its ending. A line followed by \ No newline at end of file has no ending.

Details

Lines before a file's --- header that are not part of a hunk are skipped, such as git's diff --git and index lines. A timestamp after a tab in the --- and +++ headers is dropped. A hunk must have exactly the lines its @ header counts.

Examples

d <- diff_text("a\nb\nc\n", "a\nx\nc\n")
p <- patch_parse(diff_unified(d))
p[[1]]$hunks[[1]]$lines
#>       op text
#> 1  equal  a\n
#> 2 delete  b\n
#> 3 insert  x\n
#> 4  equal  c\n
